coverage: Complete dialogue in both English editions: framing and prison speakers, named visitors and references, reviewed family/official roles and the weaver analogy; stable recognition copy.

entities.name: Socrates
entities.body: The Athenian philosopher whose final conversation in prison Phaedo recounts.

entities.name: Phaedo
entities.body: Socrates’ companion who narrates his final day to Echecrates.

entities.name: Echecrates
entities.body: The man in Phlius asking Phaedo to recount Socrates’ final hours.

entities.name: Simmias
entities.body: The Theban friend of Socrates who, with Cebes, questions him about the soul.

entities.name: Cebes
entities.body: The Theban friend of Socrates who, with Simmias, examines his arguments about the soul.

entities.name: Crito
entities.body: Socrates’ longtime friend, attending to his practical needs in prison; father of Critobulus.

entities.name: Apollodorus
entities.body: The intensely emotional friend of Socrates present in the prison.

entities.name: Xanthippe
entities.body: Socrates’ wife, visiting him in prison with their young child.

entities.name: Critobulus
entities.body: Crito’s son, one of the friends present with Socrates.

entities.name: Hermogenes
entities.body: One of Socrates’ Athenian companions present in the prison.

entities.name: Epigenes
entities.body: One of Socrates’ Athenian companions present in the prison.

entities.name: Aeschines
entities.body: The follower of Socrates present in the prison, distinct from the later Athenian orator.

entities.name: Antisthenes
entities.body: The philosopher and follower of Socrates present in the prison.

entities.name: Ctesippus
entities.body: The Athenian from Paeania listed among Socrates’ companions in prison.

entities.name: Menexenus
entities.body: One of Socrates’ companions present in the prison.

entities.name: Phaedondes
entities.body: The Theban visitor listed with Simmias and Cebes.

entities.name: Euclid of Megara
entities.body: The philosopher visiting Socrates from Megara, distinct from the later mathematician.

entities.name: Terpison
entities.body: Euclid’s fellow visitor from Megara, also known as Terpsion.

entities.name: Plato
entities.body: The philosopher who wrote this dialogue, mentioned among Socrates’ absent friends.

entities.name: Aristippus
entities.body: The follower of Socrates whom Echecrates asks about, reported to be in Aegina.

entities.name: Cleombrotus
entities.body: The acquaintance of Socrates reported to be in Aegina with Aristippus.

entities.name: Aesop
entities.body: The traditional Greek storyteller whose fables Socrates turns into verse.

entities.name: Evenus
entities.body: The poet and philosopher who asks about Socrates’ new verses.

entities.name: Philolaus
entities.body: The Pythagorean thinker whom Simmias and Cebes have heard teaching in Thebes.

entities.name: Anaxagoras
entities.body: The Greek philosopher whose account of mind and nature Socrates discusses.

entities.name: John Milton
entities.body: The English poet cited in a translator’s comparison with Comus.

entities.name: Homer
entities.body: The ancient Greek epic poet whose Odyssey is quoted.

entities.name: Aeschylus
entities.body: The Greek tragic poet whose play Telephus is cited.

entities.name: Glaucus
entities.body: The craftsman whose art is invoked as proverbial for extraordinary skill.

entities.name: Theseus
entities.body: The Athenian hero whose voyage to Crete is commemorated by the sacred ship.

entities.name: Apollo
entities.body: The Greek god honored by the mission to Delos and by Socrates’ hymn.

entities.name: Endymion
entities.body: The figure of Greek myth famous for his unending sleep.

entities.name: Penelope
entities.body: Odysseus’ wife in the Odyssey, recalled for weaving and unweaving her web.

entities.name: Heracles
entities.body: The Greek hero invoked in the comparison about needing help against two opponents.

entities.name: Iolaus
entities.body: Heracles’ companion and helper, invoked in the exchange between Socrates and Phaedo.

entities.name: Odysseus
entities.body: The hero of Homer’s Odyssey, quoted speaking sternly to his own heart.

entities.name: Harmonia
entities.body: The Theban goddess and wife of Cadmus; her name supplies a joke about Simmias’s harmony argument.

entities.name: Cadmus
entities.body: The legendary founder of Thebes and husband of Harmonia, used as a playful name for Cebes’s argument.

entities.name: Atlas
entities.body: The mythological bearer of the heavens, used in Socrates’ discussion of what supports the world.

entities.name: Asclepius
entities.body: The Greek god of healing to whom Socrates says a cock is owed.

entities.name: God
entities.body: The divine power invoked by Socrates and his companions in their discussion of the soul.

entities.name: The Eleven
entities.body: The Athenian officials responsible for prisoners and executions.

entities.name: The prison doorkeeper
entities.body: The prison official who admits Socrates’ friends on the final morning.

entities.name: The prison officer
entities.body: The servant of the Eleven who comes to announce that it is time for Socrates to drink the poison.

entities.name: The poison attendant
entities.body: The prison attendant who prepares and administers the poison.

entities.name: Crito’s servant
entities.body: The servant whom Crito sends to fetch the poison attendant.

entities.name: Crito’s attendants
entities.body: The members of Crito’s household who escort Xanthippe home.

entities.name: Socrates’ young child
entities.body: The child whom Xanthippe holds during her prison visit.

entities.name: Socrates’ sons
entities.body: The three sons of Socrates, two young and one older.

entities.name: The women of Socrates’ family
entities.body: The female relatives who visit Socrates after his bath.

entities.name: The priest of Apollo
entities.body: The priest who crowns the sacred ship before its voyage to Delos.

entities.name: The fourteen young Athenians
entities.body: The young people whom Theseus brings safely back from Crete in the recalled tradition.

entities.name: The guiding spirit
entities.body: The personal guardian who leads a soul after death in Socrates’ account.

entities.name: The weaver in Cebes’s comparison
entities.body: The imagined weaver used to compare the soul’s endurance with the body’s.
